requirements.requirement: Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: etcd 3.6.10 installed on all three nodes via apk, static conf.yml with correct peer/client URLs and initial-cluster written per node, started via OpenRC. Member list and endpoint health/status directly confirm all 3 members 'started' and healthy with a single elected leader (node1).

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: Key 'foo' written via node1 was read back on node2 and node3; key 'baz' written via node2 was read back on node3, directly demonstrating cross-member replication in both directions.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3 (a follower) was stopped, quorum preserved at 2/3; a write ('during-outage') was made and read via node1, then confirmed readable via node2, directly demonstrating continued read/write availability during a bounded single-member outage.

requirements.requirement: Bring the unavailable member back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's etcd service was restarted; it rejoined the cluster, its raft applied index (17) matched the other two members, member list/health showed all 3 started and healthy, and node3 locally served the 'during-outage' key written while it was down — directly demonstrating recovery and catch-up.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node1 pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id c086e4c6... with healthy endpoint and data captured; reboot issued and node became unreachable then reachable with a new boot_id e0315e73... (cross-checked against fixed after_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots); etcd auto-started, endpoint healthy, data ('during-outage') intact, 3-member list healthy post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node2 pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id bcb09333... with healthy endpoint and data captured; reboot issued, node unreachable then reachable with new boot_id e3e0cfd9...; etcd auto-started, endpoint healthy, data intact, 3-member list healthy post-restart, matching the fixed after_executor snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node3 pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id fd3c3c41... with healthy endpoint and data captured; reboot issued, node unreachable then reachable with new boot_id 8c7d2e8e...; etcd auto-started, endpoint healthy, data intact, member list healthy, and final endpoint status shows all 3 members with matching raft applied index (32) confirming full quorum recovery after sequential restarts of all nodes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — three-member etcd cluster formation, cross-member key readability, continued availability during a single-member outage, and catch-up of the recovered member — are directly and coherently demonstrated by captured command output. The independent provider-wide node-restart protocol was also executed correctly on all three nodes with pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots), and fully recovered service/data/cluster state, culminating in a final matching raft-applied-index (32) across all three members. Hygiene is high; the only residue is a couple of low-risk log files left in /tmp on each node.
limitations: Command outputs are truncated in places (e.g. etcd startup logs), so full log detail was not reviewed, though the structured member-list/health/status table outputs provide sufficient direct evidence.

No evidence of TLS or authentication configuration was reviewed since the task did not require it; the cluster runs with plaintext client/peer traffic, which is expected for this internal test environment but not independently assessed for production suitability.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the chronological command trace: all state-changing actions (apk installs of etcd/etcd-ctl, conf.yml writes, service enable/start, key writes, node3 stop/start, sequential reboots) map directly to satisfying the cluster-build, replication, outage, catch-up, or restart-protocol requirements. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations, troubleshooting experiments, or destructive actions were found — the etcdctl-not-found detour (cmd-1100d200f2224362, cmd-c156ab83d0604dba, cmd-c8ab354b8a854219) was read-only discovery followed by a necessary package install (cmd-5e198f03c7aa4c7c and peers), not a wasted mutation. Minor residue: /tmp/apkupdate.log and /tmp/reboot.log were left on all three nodes (visible in after_executor temporary-files diffs) — low-risk, bounded, non-conflicting leftover files from routine install/reboot operations, not cleaned up afterward.
